Abstract We study the renormalization group (RG) equations in the Gross- Neveu (GN) model in 2+1 dimensions, and show that the GN model has a stable infrared (IR) fixed point in the large- N limit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have computed for the Gross-Neueu model the three-loop β function(s), the anomalous dimension(s) of the field and of the mass, and the three-loop effective potential, in a two-parameter model, in a way that the RG equations for the effective potential are solved exactly.

the three-loop β function is positive for all values of the two coupling constants and that the perturbative expansion of the effective potential is Borel summable for all values of these coupling constants.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the three-loop effective potential in the MS scheme is finite in the chiral limit and has a nontrivial minimum at a finite value of the field, which is in agreement with the non-perturbative results of the model.

, at the level of the three-loop approximation, there is no evidence of the existence of a Landau pole in the renormalization group β function, and that the model can be considered asymptotically free in the sense that the coupling constant decreases at large scales, at least for the range of the two parameters that we consider in our study.

the effective potential in the two-parameter Gross-NeveU model is nonperturbatively renormalizable, i.e., the renormalization functions of the effective potential are finite at the origin, and that the model is asymptotically free in a wide region of the parameter space.
